previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mrs. ___ was admitted for shortness of breath, left-sided chest pain, and bilateral foot swelling. She had increased use of albuterol and nebulizers at home, with a cough producing yellow sputum and subjective chills. Evaluation revealed no acute cardiopulmonary process on chest X-ray, normal troponin, and stable labs. Her symptoms were attributed to an acute asthma exacerbation, possibly triggered by a mild respiratory infection. She was treated with a six-day prednisone taper, a five-day course of azithromycin, and continued bronchodilator therapy. Her chronic conditions, including hypertension, rheumatoid arthritis, and chronic pain, were managed with baseline medications. She improved clinically, maintained oxygen saturation on room air, and was discharged home with instructions to complete her medications, continue home inhalers, and start a nicotine patch to aid smoking cessation. Follow-up was arranged with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
Patient is a ___ female with history of breast/lung 
cancer, recently worsening asthma, and hypertension that 
presented for evaluation of headache and nausea/vomiting in 
setting of recent malaise with secondary inability to take blood 
pressure medications resulting in hypertensive emergency. 
.  
#. Hypertensive emergency:
Patient presented with headache and nausea/vomiting likely in 
the setting of hypertensive emergency as her symptoms correlated 
with her blood prssure. Neurology was consulted in the emergency 
department for some slurred speech and headache with concern for 
meningitis. Urine and serum tox was negative. Patient refused 
lumbar puncture. She was given hydral and her home medications. 
She was subsequently discharged on her home medications 
(lisinopril 30 mg PO daily, metoprolol tartrate 100 mg PO three 
times daily, valsartan 320 mg PO daily) in addition to 
Amlodipine 10 mg PO daily. With blood pressure control, her 
headache and nausea/vomiting resolved. She was subsequently 
discharged.
 
.  
#. Nausea/Vomiting
She presented with poor PO intake including medications in the 
setting of nausea. She had sick exposure to viral 
gastroenteritis from her grand children. It is likely the nausea 
and vomiting was secondary to her hypertensive emergency. Her 
LFTs and lipase were normal with benign abdominal exam. Given 
her resolution of symptoms with adequate PO intake correlated to 
blood pressure control, again this is likely secondary to her 
hypertensive urgency. 

#. Agitation and somnolence:
In the ED, the patient was still somewhat somnolent and agitated 
by the interview.  Per neurology, it is likely her altered 
mental status is mostly metabolic (possibly secondary to her 
asthma flare and narcotic use). CT head was negative with 
non-focal neurological exam. She had slurred speech that 
resolved with blood pressure control.  Her mental status 
subsequently returned to baseline. 

.  
#. Asthma: She was recently treated for an exacerbation by her 
allergist and reports she is on prednisone taper. Her asthma was 
stable in the hospital.
On discharge, she was continued on prednisone 30 mg PO daily 
with a prescription for 7 days and told to call her allergist to 
determine how to complete her taper. She likely needs to 
decrease her dosage to 20 mg PO daily. She was also continued on 
azithromycin 500 mg PO with end date on ___ per her request as 
the lower dose is not helpful. She should be weaned off 
azithromycin as well given that this type of antibiotic usage 
does not make complete sense. She was also told to call her 
allergist to discuss this. 

She was continued on albuterol and atrovent as well as advair, 
singulair and zyrtec.  Given her prolonged flair, consider beta 
blocker side effect. More rare causes of her lung issues could 
include leflunomide-induced pneumonitis although rare given CT 
chest on ___ showing left lingular ground glass opacities
